topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the key learning outcomes regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Etiology of Cancer: Genetic, Endogenous, and Environmental Influences
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how cancer arises through genetic and evolutionary processes influenced by the interplay between endogenous mutations and environmental risk factors.

topics.label: Pathogen-Driven Carcinogenesis and Burkitt Lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious pathogens drive oncogenesis, illustrated through the etiology and mechanisms of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical and chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic processing to induce DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumour Initiation and Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the distinction between mutagenic initiation and non-mutagenic promotion in driving tumour outgrowth.

topics.label: Host Susceptibility, Life Stages, and Mechanistic Summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how host life stages and tissue context influence cancer development and summarise the overall mechanisms of carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to identify carcinogens and assess their cancer-causing potential.

topics.label: Concluding Remarks on Risk and Benefit
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the lecture's closing summary on assessing carcinogenic risks versus practical benefits.
